- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., > 3 days of negative values), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecasted decline magnitude.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots downward in subsequent days; apply mild upward bias to offset lagged correction.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive price drops), model tends to overpredict further decline; adjust forecast to align with recent trend reversal.
- When sentiment is positive and price is near recent high, model often overestimates upward momentum; cap forecast growth to avoid overbought bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently underestimates volatility in early days of the horizon; increase early forecast volatility or add small upward bias if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction, not just price history.
